name: Olympus Mons summit caldera
blurb: The summit of Olympus Mons, nearly 21 km above the datum: the south rim of the caldera complex, where a three-kilometre cliff drops to the floor of the youngest collapse, the air is a seventh of the pressure below, and the sky goes dark overhead. The high, lonely end of the world.

projection.name: Equirectangular, Mars 2000 sphere, true scale at 17.9625 deg (latTs = lat0), centred on 226.75 E
projection.note: x = R cos(lat_ts) (lon - lon_0), y = R lat (radians): projected metres are true metres at the site's latitude; cos_lat0 (the world scale factor) is therefore 1

grid.convention: sample (i,j) of a level is centred at x0+(i+0.5)*mpp, y0-(j+0.5)*mpp; tile (tx,ty) holds samples tx*tile.. and ty*tile..
grid.world: game X = east metres from the site centre = x - x_centre; game Z = south metres = y_centre - y; game Y = height_m - height.ref

height.encoding: height_m = offset + (R*256 + G) * scale; B = provenance

provenance_byte.255: Mars Express HRSC DTM h0037_0000 (DA4, heights above the areoid), 50 m (50 m posts)
provenance_byte.64: Mars MGS MOLA - MEX HRSC Blended DEM Global 200 m, v2 (USGS Astrogeology) (200 m posts)
provenance_byte.0: no data (filled from the nearest valid sample)

levelling.method: each layer stretched to 8 bits once per site (0.5 / 99.5 percentiles of the first layer; later layers matched to it in mean and spread where they overlap), then feathered in priority order

ctx.title: Mars MRO CTX equirectangular mosaic MC-09, 6 m (Robbins et al., USGS Astrogeology)
ctx.composition: Context Camera (MRO CTX) images, photometrically normalised and mosaicked; 16-bit greyscale
ctx.licence: Public domain (USGS Astrogeology / NASA); credit the producers. CTX: NASA / JPL / Malin Space Science Systems. Cite Robbins et al. 2023, CTX mosaics of Mars' equatorial quadrangles (USGS Astrogeology).

colour.title: Mars Viking MDIM 2.1 colorized global mosaic, 232 m (USGS Astrogeology)
colour.composition: Viking Orbiter images (MDIM 2.1) coloured from Viking colour observations; used here only as a low-resolution colour tint
colour.licence: Public domain (USGS Astrogeology / NASA); credit the producers. Cite USGS Astrogeology, Viking MDIM 2.1 colorized mosaic (NASA / JPL / USGS).

style.name: summit lava plains and caldera scarps

tint.from: hue of the darkest, middle and brightest fifths of the Viking MDIM 2.1 colour mosaic over the site (dark and bright pulled halfway to the middle; a hue that is not red > green > blue falls back to the game's own); brightness kept from the game's default ramp

pois.name: Landing
pois.note: The summit plateau south of the caldera, 20.9 km above the datum: surface pressure about 0.1 kPa, a seventh of the planetary mean.
pois.source: Story location (fictional), placed on the real terrain model

pois.name: Caldera rim camp
pois.note: A level patch of lava a kilometre back from the south rim of the caldera complex.
pois.source: Story location (fictional), placed on the real terrain model

pois.name: The long view
pois.note: The lip of the south wall: three kilometres straight down to the floor of the youngest caldera (about 18 km above the datum), and the far walls of the older collapses beyond. The horizon here is so far below the summit that the volcano's own slopes hide the plains.
pois.source: Story location (fictional), placed on the real terrain model

pois.name: Foot of the summit climb
pois.note: Where the last of the long slope begins. The western scarp itself (six kilometres of cliff) is far below the edge of this map; the story's climb ends up here.
pois.source: Story location (fictional), placed on the real terrain model

pois.name: Top of the climb
pois.note: The rim camp: a level patch of lava a kilometre back from the caldera.
pois.source: Story location (fictional), placed on the real terrain model

pois.name: The caldera rim
pois.note: The lip of the south wall of the youngest caldera: about 2.4 km down to the floor over 4 km of 30-degree wall. The high, lonely end of the world.
pois.source: Story location (fictional), placed on the real terrain model (the first point past the long view where the wall exceeds 15 degrees)

pois.name: Caldera floor
pois.note: The flat floor of the youngest caldera, about 18.5 km above the datum.
pois.source: Real terrain (MOLA-HRSC / HRSC h0037), measured from the game's height model

notes: The layered benches in the caldera walls below 50 m and the small pit chains are generated; the walls, the nested calderas and the summit plains are the HRSC (h0037) and MOLA-HRSC terrain.
quality: HRSC stereo 50 m and MOLA-HRSC 200 m terrain; CTX 6 m imagery
